title: microdot tool offers painless permanent tattoos to those with blood and needle phobias
excerpt: a patch featuring dissolving microneedles turns digital designs into small permanent tattoos applied in fifteen minutes.
content_html:
needle punctures replaced with a dissolving patch

CipherX compresses the tattoo process into a small disposable patch filled with hundreds of pigment-carrying microneedles. Applied with a handheld tool, the patch stays on the skin for around 10 to 15 minutes while its microscopic points dissolve and deposit ink in a fixed digital pattern, removing the vibration, visible blood, and repeated puncturing associated with a conventional tattoo machine.

The system gives permanent body art a different point of entry, especially for people who find the standard process physically or psychologically inaccessible. Materials scientist and designer Ferdinand Kohle develops the original concept around his own needle and blood phobia, asking whether biomedical microneedle technology could deliver a permanent image with minimal discomfort.


CipherX replaces the conventional tattoo machine with a single-use microneedle patch | images © CipherX

from tattoo machine to microdot patch

Once the patch is aligned, the applicator presses its microscopic points through the upper layers of skin in a single motion. Each microdot combines biodegradable material with tattoo pigment, turning the patch into both an image carrier and a delivery system.

It remains secured to the body while the structures dissolve, and leaves the pigment behind in a fixed arrangement. Microneedle tattoo patches have appeared in academic research since at least 2022, but the team at CipherX is turning the principle into a manufactured consumer product.

Although the first image appears as soon as the patch is removed, it can look pale during the opening hours. The marks deepen over the next two days and visually merge into a continuous form. CipherX describes the experience as pain-free, while its public guidance also mentions temporary redness or mild irritation. Aftercare involves petroleum jelly and avoiding prolonged water exposure for the first 48 hours.


the dedicated applicator positions the patch and applies pressure in one motion

a permanent image built from microdots

For CipherX, the pixel offers a useful model for translating digital artwork into a permanent image on skin. A file becomes a field of pigment-filled microdots, then a disposable patch whose microscopic points reproduce the pattern on the body. This gives the tattoo a strange material sequence. It moves from screen to mold, then from patch to skin.

By shifting much of the image-making process into software and manufacturing, the system changes the familiar relationship between a wearer and the tattooing process. A conventional tattoo develops through the movement of a hand across skin. Here, the design arrives prearranged, and the applicator controls alignment and pressure through one repeatable action. CipherX received the Red Dot Best of the Best award for the applicator in 2026.


each patch remains on the skin for around fifteen minutes

a personal question becomes a skin technology company

Materials scientist and designer Ferdinand Kohle began exploring the idea in late 2020 while studying Innovation Design Engineering at the Royal College of Art and Imperial College London. ‘I was interested in tattoos but found conventional tattooing inaccessible because of my needle and blood phobia,‘ he explains.

His technical background gave the question a practical direction: could dissolving microneedles move permanent pigment into skin through a single application?

After Kohle founded CipherX with clinician and researcher Karl-Anton Harms, tattooing became the first commercial use for a wider skin technology platform. The company is also exploring cosmetic treatments and medical marking, alongside drug delivery and health sensing.

For now, Microdot Tattoos remain available through approved pop-ups and trained practitioners. Home application sits further along the company’s roadmap, where the patch could move tattooing beyond the studio and into retail spaces or live events.


hundreds of pigment-filled microdots form each permanent image


the tattoo darkens and becomes more visible over the following two days

content_html_zh:
用溶解贴片代替针刺

CipherX 将纹身过程压缩成一个小的一次性贴片，其中充满了数百个携带颜料的微针。 使用手持工具使用时，贴片会在皮肤上停留约 10 至 15 分钟，同时其微观点会溶解并以固定的数字图案沉积墨水，从而消除与传统纹身机相关的振动、可见血液和重复刺穿。

该系统为永久性人体艺术提供了不同的切入点，特别是对于那些在身体或心理上难以接受标准流程的人来说。 材料科学家兼设计师费迪南德·科尔 (Ferdinand Kohle) 围绕自己的针头和血液恐惧症开发了最初的概念，询问生物医学微针技术是否可以在最小化不适的情况下提供永久图像。

CipherX 用一次性微针贴片取代传统纹身机 |图片©CipherX

从纹身机到微点贴片

一旦贴片对齐，敷贴器就会通过一次动作将其微观点压过皮肤上层。 每个微粒将可生物降解的材料与纹身颜料结合在一起，将贴片变成图像载体和传输系统。

当结构溶解时，它仍然固定在身体上，并将颜料留在固定的排列中。 微针纹身贴至少从 2022 年起就出现在学术研究中，但 CipherX 团队正在将这一原理转化为制造消费品。

虽然第一张图像在贴片被移除后立即出现，但在开放时间内它可能看起来很苍白。 在接下来的两天里，这些标记会加深，并在视觉上融合成一个连续的形式。 CipherX 将这种体验描述为无痛，而其公共指导也提到了暂时的发红或轻度刺激。 术后护理包括使用凡士林并避免在前 48 小时内长时间接触水。

专用涂抹器一次定位贴片并施加压力

由微粒构建的永久图像

对于 CipherX 来说，像素提供了一个有用的模型，可以将数字艺术作品转化为皮肤上的永久图像。 锉刀变成了充满颜料的微粒区域，然后是一次性贴片，其微粒在身体上再现了图案。 这给纹身带来了奇怪的材料序列。 它从屏幕移动到模具，然后从贴片移动到皮肤。

通过将大部分图像制作过程转移到软件和制造中，该系统改变了佩戴者和纹身过程之间熟悉的关系。 传统的纹身是通过手在皮肤上的移动而形成的。 在这里，设计是预先安排好的，涂抹器通过一个可重复的动作来控制对齐和压力。 CipherX 的涂抹器于 2026 年荣获红点最佳应用奖。

每个贴片在皮肤上保留约十五分钟

一个个人问题成为一家皮肤科技公司

材料科学家兼设计师 Ferdinand Kohle 于 2020 年底在皇家艺术学院和伦敦帝国理工学院学习创新设计工程时开始探索这一想法。 “我对纹身很感兴趣，但由于我对针和血的恐惧，我发现传统的纹身无法进行，”他解释道。

他的技术背景为这个问题提供了一个实用的方向：溶解微针能否通过单次应用将永久性色素转移到皮肤中？

Kohle 与临床医生兼研究员 Karl-Anton Harms 创立 CipherX 后，纹身成为更广泛的皮肤技术平台的第一个商业用途。 该公司还在探索美容治疗和医疗标记，以及药物输送和健康传感。

目前，微点纹身仍然可以通过经批准的弹出窗口和训练有素的从业者获得。 家庭应用程序位于公司路线图的更远处，该补丁可以将纹身从工作室转移到零售空间或现场活动中。

每个永久图像由数百个充满颜料的微粒形成

在接下来的两天里，纹身会变暗并变得更加明显
